name: HumanLayer
tagline: SDKs and local tools for human approval and oversight of AI agents.
hook: A two-part monorepo guide tracing the approval protocol, SDK platform, local tools, package workflows, and implementation stages.
summary: HumanLayer's CLAUDE.md distinguishes the SDK platform from local tools for approvals and coding sessions. A protocol diagram traces the flow, while language-specific sections and numbered TODO levels guide implementation.

techniques.title: Show the approval path across processes
techniques.body: An architecture diagram follows Claude Code through MCP, the CLI, the daemon, and the cloud API. It also shows where terminal and graphical approval interfaces join the flow.
techniques.quote:
### Architecture Flow
```
Claude Code → MCP Protocol → hlyr → JSON-RPC → hld → HumanLayer Cloud API
                                         ↑         ↑
                                    TUI ─┘         └─ WUI
```

techniques.title: Read package-local tool choices
techniques.body: The TypeScript guidance avoids assuming one package manager or test framework throughout the monorepo. It directs those choices to package.json scripts and dependencies.
techniques.quote:
### TypeScript Development
- Package managers vary - check `package.json` for npm or bun
- Build/test commands differ - check `package.json` scripts section
- Some use Jest, others Vitest, check `package.json` devDependencies

techniques.title: Name what each TODO priority means
techniques.body: The annotation vocabulary distinguishes critical blockers, architectural issues, feature gaps, polish, and open questions. The critical level explicitly means work must not merge.
techniques.quote:
We use a priority-based TODO annotation system throughout the codebase:

- `TODO(0)`: Critical - never merge
- `TODO(1)`: High - architectural flaws, major bugs
- `TODO(2)`: Medium - minor bugs, missing features
- `TODO(3)`: Low - polish, tests, documentation
- `TODO(4)`: Questions/investigations needed
- `PERF`: Performance optimization opportunities

steal: Show how requests cross process and protocol boundaries.
Use package manifests as the authority when tools vary within a monorepo.
Define a shared priority vocabulary for TODOs.
